system:
You draft public Twitter replies for Spotify's customer support account (@SpotifyCares), in 2017.

You will be given a customer's message and a numbered list of PRECEDENTS: real past customer messages with the reply Spotify actually sent. Your reply must be consistent with those precedents.

Hard rules:
- Ground every factual claim in the precedents. If the precedents do not establish something, do not say it.
- Never invent a policy, price, timeframe, refund, or entitlement.
- Never promise an action Spotify would have to take on the customer's account (refunding, resetting, unlocking, cancelling). You cannot see their account.
- If the precedents mainly ask the customer for more information, then asking for that same information IS the correct reply.
- Match the register of the precedents: warm, brief, lower-case-friendly, first person plural. Under 280 characters.
- If the precedents do not actually address the customer's problem, say so honestly in the `reply` and give a low confidence.

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"reply": "<the reply text>", "confidence": <0.0-1.0>, "evidence_ids": ["<ids you used>"]}

`confidence` is how well the precedents support your reply, not how fluent it is.
prompt:
CUSTOMER MESSAGE:
my sister registered to Spotify with my bank account and she can't seem to remember her email nor her password. Is it possibly for me to cancel my subscription?

PREDICTED INTENT: subscription_manage

PRECEDENTS:

[2251784] (similarity 0.70, intent subscription_manage)
  past customer: I️ need to contact someone about cancelling a membership that was used with my card. I️ have never used Spotify! #GetAContactNumber
  spotify replied: 2: your statement? It usually starts with "P03". We'll take a look backstage /GT <link>

[620416] (similarity 0.62, intent subscription_manage)
  past customer: am I right in thinking that to change the billing date on my Spotify Premium account I have to cancel and then signup again on the day I want the money to come out? This does seem a very stupid way of doing it!!!
  spotify replied: Hi there. We're sorry you feel that way. Right now, that is the only way to change your monthly billing date for your Premium subscription. We appreciate your feedback on this, and we'll be sure to pass it on to the right folks

[2128548] (similarity 0.61, intent subscription_manage)
  past customer: Hi I renewed my subscription by accident. But account still shows expired. Who can I email details to?
  spotify replied: Hey James! We'd be happy to lend a hand via Twitter. But if you'd prefer, you can email us at __email__

[162237] (similarity 0.60, intent subscription_manage)
  past customer: Hi I didn't have enough money in my bank account linked to my Spotify premium and was put back to free. I have since payed it and my iTunes says that it's active but the app won't allow me to access premium only the free subscription. I'm on iOs __email__
  spotify replied: It seems the system was unable to process your payment. We'd recommend reaching out to iTunes for more information on the charge. Any other questions, feel free to give us a shout

[2537560] (similarity 0.60, intent subscription_manage)
  past customer: I want to reactivate my Spotify account can you help me please
  spotify replied: Hi Christopher! Could you send us your account's email address? We'll take a look backstage

Draft the reply as JSON.
